tasks.description: Create src/todo-store.js (persistence) and src/todo-format.js (pure list rendering) so the data file format and the output format are decided in exactly one place. edits.change:
New ESM module importing { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, renameSync } from 'node:fs', path from 'node:path' and os from 'node:os'. Export exactly these named functions:
- `todoFilePath()` — returns process.env.TODO_FILE when it is a non-empty string, else path.join(os.homedir(), '.todos.json').
- `loadTodos(file = todoFilePath())` — if the file is missing return []; otherwise JSON.parse it, require an array result, and throw new Error(`Could not parse todos file: ${file}`) on invalid JSON.
- `saveTodos(todos, file = todoFilePath())` — write JSON.stringify(todos, null, 2) + '\n' to `${file}.tmp` then renameSync it over `file` (atomic replace).
- `addTodo(text, file = todoFilePath())` — trim text, push `{ id, text, done: false }` where id is (max existing id + 1, or 1 when the list is empty), save, return the new todo.
- `completeTodo(id, file = todoFilePath())` — find the todo with that id, set done = true, save, return it.
- `removeTodo(id, file = todoFilePath())` — find the index, splice the todo out, save, return the removed todo.
completeTodo and removeTodo return null and write nothing when no todo has that id.

New ESM module with two exported pure functions and no fs access:
- `formatTodoLine(todo)` returns the string `` `${todo.done ? '[x]' : '[ ]'} ${todo.id} ${todo.text}` ``.
- `formatList(todos)` returns a multi-line string: when `todos` is empty return the single line 'No todos.'; otherwise every line from formatTodoLine joined with '\n', then a blank line, then `${todos.length} item(s) (${done} done, ${pending} pending)` counting done and pending entries.

node:test file that before each test creates a fresh temp directory under the project with fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(process.cwd(), '.tmp-todo-')) and sets process.env.TODO_FILE to path.join(thatDir, '.todos.json'), and in the after hook restores the previous TODO_FILE value and calls fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }). Cover: addTodo appends and returns { id: 1, text: 'buy milk', done: false } with surrounding whitespace trimmed; ids keep incrementing across adds; the file on disk parses back to the same array; completeTodo flips done to true; removeTodo removes the entry and drops it from the file; completeTodo and removeTodo return null for an unknown id and leave the file untouched; loadTodos on a missing file returns []; loadTodos on a file holding invalid JSON throws; formatTodoLine returns '[ ] 1 buy milk' for a pending todo and '[x] 1 buy milk' for a done one; formatList on [] returns 'No todos.'.

edits.change:
New ESM module importing { addTodo, completeTodo, removeTodo, loadTodos } from './todo-store.js' and { formatList } from './todo-format.js'. Top-level constant `export const USAGE` set to the multi-line string:
Usage: todo <command> [args]

Commands:
  add <text>       Add a todo
  list [--pending]  List todos (--pending hides done ones)
  done <id>         Mark a todo as done
  remove <id>       Remove a todo
Export `async function run(argv, io = console)` where io provides { out(line), err(line) }.

Argument handling: the first element that is not a flag (does not start with '--') is the command, the remaining non-flag elements are its arguments, and '--pending' is a flag.
- `add` — with no arguments call io.err(USAGE) and return 1; otherwise `const todo = addTodo(args.join(' '))`, io.out(`Added ${todo.id} ${todo.text}`), return 0.
- `list` — `const all = loadTodos()`, `const todos = flags.includes('--pending') ? all.filter(t => !t.done) : all`, io.out(formatList(todos)), return 0.
- `done` — if args[0] is missing or Number.isNaN(Number(args[0])), io.err(USAGE) and return 1; otherwise `const todo = completeTodo(Number(args[0]))`; when it is null io.err(`No todo with id ${args[0]}`) and return 1, else io.out(`Marked done: ${todo.id} ${todo.text}`) and return 0.
- `remove` — identical id parsing to `done`; `removeTodo(Number(args[0]))`; when null io.err(`No todo with id ${args[0]}`) and return 1, else io.out(`Removed ${todo.id} ${todo.text}`) and return 0.
- Any other command, or none at all — io.err(USAGE), return 1.

At the very bottom of the file add the only side effect: `if (process.argv[1] && process.argv[1].endsWith('todo-cli.js')) { try { process.exitCode = await run(process.argv.slice(2)) } catch (e) { console.error(e.message); process.exitCode = 1 } }` so importing the module in tests never executes it.

# demo

A small Node project with a `todo` command-line tool.

## todo

Todos are stored as JSON in `~/.todos.json`. Set the `TODO_FILE` environment variable to store
them somewhere else. Run the tool with the npm script: `npm run todo -- <command>`.

    npm run todo -- add buy milk
    npm run todo -- list
    npm run todo -- done 1
    npm run todo -- remove 1

`list` prints one todo per line as `<mark> <id> <text>`, where the mark is `[x]` for a done todo
and `[ ]` for a pending one, followed by a summary line. Pass `--pending` to hide done todos:

    npm run todo -- list --pending

Ids start at 1. An unknown command, a missing argument or an unknown id prints the usage text and
exits with status 1.

contracts.statement: A todo item is exactly `{ id: number, text: string, done: boolean }`. The store file (~/.todos.json, or $TODO_FILE when set) contains a JSON array of these items, pretty-printed with 2-space indent and a trailing newline, written atomically (write a sibling temp file, then rename). If the file does not exist it is read as an empty list; if it exists but holds invalid JSON, loading throws an Error whose message mentions the file path.

`list` prints one item per line as `<mark> <id> <text>` with no trailing spaces, where mark is '[x]' when the item is done and '[ ]' when it is pending, followed by a final summary line `<n> item(s) (<m> done, <k> pending)`. Empty lists print `No todos.` and omit the summary. `add <text>` prints `Added <id> <text>`. `done <id>` prints `Marked done: <id> <text>`. `remove <id>` prints `Removed <id> <text>`. Every unknown command, missing argument or unparsable id prints a usage block listing add/list/done/remove to stderr and returns exit code 1; every successful command returns 0.

Every store entry point resolves the data file the same way: if process.env.TODO_FILE is a non-empty string use exactly that path, otherwise use path.join(os.homedir(), '.todos.json'). No code path may write to the real home directory when TODO_FILE is set, and tests must always point TODO_FILE at a temp directory created inside the project.
